# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Albacetire for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## The Mining Years Albacetire was settled for what lies under its ravines and rolling hills. Through the 2160s the mining concerns moved heavier and heavier equipment into the deep ravines, and the colony was already pulling in billions. Safety spending did not keep pace with the drilling.
## The Ravine Incident, 2168 - During a routine deep-core dig, Drill Site 68-B broke into a sealed ravine system full of pressurised carbon monoxide and other volatile gases. - More than 1,200 miners suffocated in the tunnels within minutes. There was no plan for a leak of that size. - A wind shift drove the cloud over the mining camp, the township and the old garrison. Residential blocks were lost, responders could not hold it back and vehicles stalled in the streets. - By the time orbital monitors picked up the bloom it was too late. The official toll passed [bold]12,000[/bold] before the wind turned again and thinned it out. Colonial Marines, Royal Marines and Company staff were among the dead.
## The Stability Mandate UNISC came in for the humanitarian work, alongside relief from the United Americas, the Three World Empire and Weyland-Yutani. Under pressure from across human space, the three signed the [bold]Albacetire Stability Mandate[/bold]: money for infrastructure, safety and security, and a joint fortress to watch over all of it.
## Joint Base Schaefer The fort was raised in the mountains on the ruins of the old UA garrison. It houses the Colonial Marines, the Royal Marine Commandos and Weyland-Yutani PMC contractors, and it answers dissident trouble and mass emergencies, watches the air and the rock, and above all guards the colony's assets. Locals call it [bold]Stable[/bold]. Whether that is affection or a joke depends on who you ask.
## The Boom - New high-tech mines opened, and great greenhouse domes went up over the rich soil. - Money followed: investors, businesspeople, researchers and the students of the [bold]University of Albacetire[/bold]. - The population climbed to around 1,250,000, and by 2178 Albacetire ranked among the most vital economies in the Neroid Sector.
The Herald was there for all of it, and we keep the archive so that nobody gets to forget the first part.
